questions.question: A and B started a business together. A invested Rs. 36000 for 8 months while B invested some capital for 6 months. In the end B got 15/31 of the total profit, then how much money did B invest?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total profit units = 31; **B's profit** = 15 units → **A's profit** = 31 − 15 = 16 units.

Profit Ratio (A : B) = 16 : 15.

Ratio of (Investment × Time): (36000 × 8) : (B × 6) = 16 : 15.

288000 : 6B = 16 : 15 ⇒ 48000 : B = 16 : 15.

16 units = 48000 ⇒ 1 unit = 3000.

B's investment = 15 × 3000 = 45000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹45000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Investment of **A** (IA) = ₹ 36000; Time of **A** (TA) = 8 months.

Time of **B** (TB) = 6 months; Profit share of **B** = 15/31 of Total Profit.

**Formula Used:**

Ratio of Profits = Ratio of (Investment × Time)

PA ÷ PB = (IA × TA) ÷ (IB × TB)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/440858457035bd55f3e6139eb849f1dc8b4d26a4832185ee306517bf28c44dc8.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the total profit be 31 units.

⇒ Profit of **B** (PB) = 15 units.

⇒ Profit of **A** (PA) = 31 − 15 = 16 units.

⇒ Ratio PA : PB = 16 : 15.

⇒ (36000 × 8) ÷ (IB × 6) = 16 ÷ 15

⇒ 288000 ÷ 6IB = 16 ÷ 15

⇒ 48000 ÷ IB = 16 ÷ 15

⇒ 16 × IB = 48000 × 15

⇒ IB = (48000 × 15) ÷ 16

⇒ IB = 3000 × 15

⇒ IB = 45000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹45000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Partnership

In a simple partnership, all partners invest their capital for the same period of time. The profit is distributed in the ratio of their **investments**.

Compound Partnership

In a compound partnership, partners invest different amounts for different periods of time. Profit is divided in the ratio of the **product of capital and time**.

Working vs Sleeping Partner

A **Working Partner** manages the business and may receive a salary or extra profit share, while a **Sleeping Partner** only provides capital.

Investment Calculation

Capital Ratio = (Profit ÷ Time) Ratio. This is used when profit shares and time periods are known to find the capital ratio.

questions.question: If interest be compounded half - yearly, then find the compound interest on ₹8,000 at 20% p.a. for 1 year.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **half-yearly** compounding, the rate becomes **half** (20% ÷ 2 = 10%) and time **doubles** (1 × 2 = 2 periods).

Using the **Successive Percentage** formula for 2 periods of 10%:

Effective Rate = 10 + 10 + (10 × 10)/100 = **21%**

Compound Interest = 21% of 8,000 = 8,000 × 21/100 = **₹1,680**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,680.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Principal (P) = ₹8,000, Annual Rate (R) = 20%, Time (T) = 1 year.

**Formula Used:** Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ; CI = A − P

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2034bb2cb1bdf8e20076a9431cc5757c97c00e3cd5c60246ad897093605418a5.png] 

⇒ Half-yearly rate (r) = 20% ÷ 2 = 10% per half-year.

⇒ Number of half-years (n) = 1 × 2 = 2.

⇒ A = 8,000 × (1 + 10/100)²

⇒ A = 8,000 × (11/10) × (11/10)

⇒ A = 8,000 × 1.21 = ₹9,680

⇒ Compound Interest (CI) = A − P = 9,680 − 8,000

⇒ CI = ₹1,680

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,680.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate for Half-Yearly Compounding

If the annual rate is R, the effective annual rate for half-yearly compounding is [ (1 + R/200)² − 1 ] × 100.

CI vs SI for 2 Periods

The difference between CI and SI for 2 periods is P × (r/100)², where r is the rate per period.

Compounding Frequency

For quarterly compounding, divide the annual rate by 4 and multiply the time in years by 4 to get the number of periods.

questions.question: A hall is 18 m long and 12 m broad. If the area of the floor is equal to the sum of the areas of the four walls, the volume (in m³) of the hall is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of Floor = Sum of Areas of 4 Walls

L × B = 2H(L + B)

H = (L × B) ÷ [2 × (L + B)] = (18 × 12) ÷ [2 × (18 + 12)]

H = 216 ÷ 60 = 3.6 m

Volume = L × B × H = 18 × 12 × 3.6 = 777.6 m³

**∴ The correct answer is 777.6 m³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length (L) = 18 m

Breadth (B) = 12 m

**Formula Used:**

Area of Floor = L × B

Area of 4 Walls = 2 × Height (H) × (L + B)

Volume = L × B × H

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5c5a131e117ec6ceff35296bc9772d8ff1e40c45e7e779fa342d4b2f808fdbe0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of floor = 18 × 12 = 216 m²

⇒ Area of 4 walls = 2 × H × (18 + 12) = 2 × H × 30 = 60H m²

⇒ According to the question: 216 = 60H

⇒ H = 216 ÷ 60 = 3.6 m

⇒ Volume of the hall = L × B × H

⇒ Volume = 18 × 12 × 3.6

⇒ Volume = 216 × 3.6 = 777.6 m³

**∴ The correct answer is 777.6 m³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Lateral Surface Area of a Cuboid

It is the sum of the areas of the four walls, calculated as 2H(L + B).

Total Surface Area (TSA)

TSA includes the floor and the ceiling: 2(LB + BH + HL).

Volume of a Cuboid

The total space occupied by the cuboid, calculated by the product of its dimensions: Volume = L × B × H.

Diagonal of a Cuboid

The longest rod that can be placed in a hall: Diagonal = √(L² + B² + H²).</p

questions.question: From a point Q, the length of the tangent to a circle is 40 cm and the distance of Q from the centres is 41 cm. The radius of the circle is _______ cm.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The radius, the tangent, and the line joining the center to the external point form a **right-angled triangle**.

Using the common **Pythagorean triplet** (9, 40, 41):

Radius² + Tangent² = Distance²

r² + 40² = 41²

r² = 1681 − 1600 = 81

r = √81 = 9 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the **tangent** (QT) = 40 cm

Distance of point Q from the **center** (OQ) = 41 cm

**Formula used:**

In a circle, the tangent at any point is **perpendicular** to the radius through the point of contact. By **Pythagoras Theorem**: Radius² + Tangent² = (Distance from center)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cf1f7085e3c0309b8a4540db4ba370817a85a0d44dece4bfbf8821e1b547820b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **O** be the center of the circle and **T** be the point of contact of the tangent from **Q**.

⇒ In right-angled Δ**OTQ**, ∠**OTQ** = 90°.

⇒ OT² + QT² = OQ²

⇒ r² + 40² = 41²

⇒ r² + 1600 = 1681

⇒ r² = 1681 − 1600

⇒ r² = 81

⇒ r = √81 = 9 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 9 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Tangent-Radius Property

The radius of a circle is always perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact, forming a 90° angle.

Pythagorean Triplets

Sets of three integers (a, b, c) that satisfy a² + b² = c², such as (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (9, 40, 41).

Length of Tangent

The length of a tangent from an external point is calculated as L = √(d² − r²), where d is the distance from the center and r is the radius.</p

questions.question: During a festival sale, an air-conditioner is sold at Rs. 19,750 at a discount of 21%. What is its marked price (in Rs.)?

**Discount** = 21% → **Selling Price** = 100% − 21% = 79%.

Given 79% = 19750.

100% = (19750 ÷ 79) × 100 = 250 × 100 = 25000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹25000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Discount** percentage = 21%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a5723ddf28e74df7a34aa0a68559235abc74a7f2c685b36a2d164188dac2e439.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Marked Price** = [19750 × 100] ÷ [100 − 21]

⇒ **Marked Price** = [19750 × 100] ÷ 79

⇒ **Marked Price** = 250 × 100

⇒ **Marked Price** = 25000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹25000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

The price listed on the product by the manufacturer or retailer before any reduction is applied.

Discount Relation

Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price** unless stated otherwise. Discount = MP − SP.

Successive Discounts

If two discounts d₁% and d₂% are given, effective discount = [d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂)/100]%.

In parallel lines **AB** and **CD** intersected by transversal **PQ**:

∠ALM = ∠CMQ = 48° (**Corresponding Angles** are equal).

Since **PQ** is a straight line, ∠PLA and ∠ALM form a **Linear Pair**.

∠PLA + ∠ALM = 180°

⇒ ∠PLA = 180° − 48° = 132°.

**∴ The correct answer is 132°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Line **AB** || Line **CD**

⇒ Transversal **PQ** intersects **AB** at **L** and **CD** at **M**.

⇒ ∠CMQ = 48°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e9b1e510e5bd9a76077ac36537e90f1036f170b01eb482ee837964d734e410b8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ ∠LMC + ∠CMQ = 180° (Linear pair on line CD)

⇒ ∠LMC = 180° − 48° = 132°

⇒ ∠PLA and ∠LMC are **Corresponding Angles** because AB || CD and PQ is the transversal.

⇒ ∠PLA = ∠LMC

⇒ ∠PLA = 132°

**∴ The correct answer is 132°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Corresponding Angles

When two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, the angles in matching corners are equal.

Linear Pair Postulate

If two angles form a linear pair, then the measures of the angles add up to 180°.

Alternate Interior Angles

Angles between the parallel lines on opposite sides of the transversal are equal (∠ALM = ∠LMD).

Consecutive Interior Angles

Angles between the parallel lines on the same side of the transversal are supplementary (∠ALM + ∠LMC = 180°).</p

questions.question: If 257x8 is divisible by 11, what will be the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **divisibility rule of 11**: Sum of digits at odd places − Sum of digits at even places = 0 or a multiple of 11.

For the number **257x8**, digits at odd positions (1st, 3rd, 5th) are 2, 7, and 8.

Sum of odd positions = 2 + 7 + 8 = 17. Sum of even positions = 5 + x.

Difference = 17 − (5 + x) = 12 − x.

For 12 − x to be 11, x must be 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The five-digit number is **257x8** and it is divisible by **11**.

**Formula Used:** A number is divisible by 11 if the absolute difference between the sum of digits at odd positions and the sum of digits at even positions is 0, 11, 22, and so on.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b5de35eacc3f7f7398aa6f81cd761c059f4510d526634d0739ae8605cc6d0df1.png] 

⇒ Sum of digits at **odd positions** = 2 + 7 + 8 = 17

⇒ Sum of digits at **even positions** = 5 + x

⇒ Difference = 17 − (5 + x) = 12 − x

⇒ For divisibility by 11, the difference must be a multiple of 11 (0, 11, 22...).

⇒ 12 − x = 11

⇒ x = 12 − 11

⇒ x = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 3

A number is divisible by 3 if the **sum of all its digits** is divisible by 3.

Divisibility by 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the **sum of all its digits** is divisible by 9.

Divisibility by 11 Logic

If the difference between the alternating sums of digits is divisible by 11, the original number is also divisible by 11.</p

questions.question: If x+(1)/(x)=7, find the value of x³+(1)/(x³).
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If **x + 1/x = k**, then the value of **x³ + 1/x³** is calculated as **k³ − 3k**.

Given: **x + 1/x = 7**, so **k = 7**.

Calculation: 7³ − 3(7) = 343 − 21 = **322**.

**∴ The correct answer is 322.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** x + 1/x = 7

**Formula Used:** (a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a1d129dd72524e528cdcc0ece59051eb8097c47ac0b1b6e98b4b0156efe691bc.png] 

⇒ (x + 1/x)³ = 7³

⇒ x³ + (1/x)³ + 3 × x × (1/x) × (x + 1/x) = 343

⇒ x³ + 1/x³ + 3 × 1 × (7) = 343

⇒ x³ + 1/x³ + 21 = 343

⇒ x³ + 1/x³ = 343 − 21

⇒ x³ + 1/x³ = 322

**∴ The correct answer is 322.**

**__Additional Information__**

Square Relation

If x + 1/x = k, then x² + 1/x² = k² − 2. For k = 7, x² + 1/x² = 47.

Negative Sign Transformation

If x − 1/x = k, then the cubic expansion is x³ − 1/x³ = k³ + 3k.

Fourth Power Relation

If x + 1/x = k, then x⁴ + 1/x⁴ = (k² − 2)² − 2.

Algebraic Identity

a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²). Using this, x³ + 1/x³ = (x + 1/x)(x² − 1 + 1/x²).</p

In a right-angled triangle, the two acute angles are **complementary** (their sum is 90°).

From the property of the **altitude** BD ⊥ AC, triangle ADE is a right-angled triangle at D.

Given the internal angle ∠DAE = 10° from the figure geometry.

⇒ ∠AED = 90° − 10° = 80°.

Since the point B lies on the line segment ED (or ray ED), the angle ∠AEB is equal to ∠AED.

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** BD ⊥ AC, which implies ∠ADB = 90°. Point E lies on the altitude BD. From the provided geometry, ∠DAE = 10°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/41b7859aa35a2d549a10f2a013e9c34d5d6d28d875a65ac59d7c34673d029f3c.png] 

In **▵ADE**, the sum of all internal angles must be 180°.

⇒ ∠DAE + ∠ADE + ∠AED = 180°

⇒ 10° + 90° + ∠AED = 180°

⇒ 100° + ∠AED = 180°

⇒ ∠AED = 180° − 100°

⇒ ∠AED = 80°

Since points **B, E, and D** are collinear on the same perpendicular line, ∠AEB is the same as ∠AED (assuming B is positioned such that E is the vertex of the angle formed with ray EB).

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**

Complementary Angles in Right Triangle

Orthocenter Property

questions.question: What is the difference between the LCM and the HCF of 24 and 18?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the **HCF** of 24 and 18 by checking the largest number dividing both: **6**.

Find the **LCM** using the ratio method: 24 : 18 → 4 : 3. LCM = 24 × 3 = **72**.

Required Difference = LCM − HCF = 72 − 6 = 66.

**∴ The correct answer is 66.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The numbers are 24 and 18.

**Formula Used:** Difference = LCM(a, b) − HCF(a, b)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7b3041260f47ffc70d41e9ba6b36a1f2991e5e16b4f3b0d935f6255d03c426bd.png] 

⇒ Prime factorization of 24 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 2³ × 3¹

⇒ Prime factorization of 18 = 2 × 3 × 3 = 2¹ × 3²

⇒ **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** = 2¹ × 3¹ = 6

⇒ **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** = 2³ × 3² = 8 × 9 = 72

⇒ Required Difference = 72 − 6 = 66

**∴ The correct answer is 66.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Rule of LCM and HCF

The product of two numbers is always equal to the product of their **LCM** and **HCF** (a × b = LCM × HCF).

Co-prime Numbers

For any two **co-prime numbers**, the HCF is always 1 and the LCM is the product of the two numbers.

HCF and LCM Relation

The **HCF** of any group of numbers is always a factor of their **LCM**.</p

questions.question: The radius of a cone and a sphere are same i.e. 15 cm. If the volume of the cone and the sphere are also same, then find the height of the cone.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When the **radius (r)** and **volume** of a **cone** and **sphere** are the same:

(1/3) × π × r² × h = (4/3) × π × r³

By simplifying the relation, we get **h = 4 × r**.

Given **r = 15 cm**, the **height (h)** of the cone is 4 × 15.

**h = 60 cm**.

**∴ The correct answer is 60 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Radius of cone (r꜀)** = 15 cm

**Radius of sphere (rₛ)** = 15 cm

**Volume of cone (V꜀)** = **Volume of sphere (Vₛ)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/56d694bb7bd496b26dfa231d5b6fd9c9ed2391787f9959ee4d60240545821850.png] 

**Formula Used:**

**Volume of Cone** = (1/3) × π × r² × h

**Volume of Sphere** = (4/3) × π × r³

**Calculations:**

⇒ (1/3) × π × (15)² × h = (4/3) × π × (15)³

⇒ (1/3) × 225 × h = (4/3) × 3375

⇒ 225 × h = 4 × 3375

⇒ h = (4 × 3375) ÷ 225

⇒ h = 4 × 15

⇒ h = 60 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 60 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Slant Height of Cone

The slant height (l) is given by the Pythagorean relation: l = √(r² + h²).

Curved Surface Area of Cone

The curved surface area is given by π × r × l, where l is the slant height.

Surface Area of Sphere

The total surface area of a sphere is 4 × π × r².

Volume of Cylinder

The volume of a cylinder with the same radius and height is π × r² × h, which is thrice the volume of the cone.</p

questions.question: The mean and mode of a set of data are 58.7 and 61.1, respectively. Find the median of the data, using the empirical formula.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **empirical relationship** between central tendencies is: 3 × **Median** = **Mode** + 2 × **Mean**

3 × Median = 61.1 + 2 × 58.7

3 × Median = 61.1 + 117.4 = 178.5

Median = 178.5 ÷ 3 = 59.5

**∴ The correct answer is 59.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Mean** of the data = 58.7

**Mode** of the data = 61.1

Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/677f028b625b7155f9508dc8035e0d044f1b0e6636299c6ff6d900bbf5d3c00a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 61.1 = 3 × Median − 2 × 58.7

⇒ 61.1 = 3 × Median − 117.4

⇒ 3 × Median = 61.1 + 117.4

⇒ 3 × Median = 178.5

⇒ Median = 178.5 ÷ 3

⇒ Median = 59.5

**∴ The correct answer is 59.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Symmetric Distribution

In a perfectly **symmetrical distribution**, the Mean, Median, and Mode are all equal (Mean = Median = Mode).

Positive Skewness

In a **positively skewed** distribution, the values generally follow the order: Mean > Median > Mode.

Negative Skewness

In a **negatively skewed** distribution, the values generally follow the order: Mode > Median > Mean.

Empirical Rule Scope

The relationship **Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean** is an approximation used for moderately skewed unimodal distributions.</p

questions.question: If x + y = 1 and x² + y² = 41, then what is the value of (1)/(x) + (1)/(y)?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identify the product **xy** using 2xy = (x + y)² − (x² + y²).

2xy = 1² − 41 = −40 ⇒ **xy = −20**.

The expression **1/x + 1/y** simplifies to (x + y) / xy.

Substituting the values: 1 / (−20) = **−1/20**.

**∴ The correct answer is − 1/20.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of terms: **x + y = 1**

Sum of squares: **x² + y² = 41**

**Formula Used:**

Algebraic Identity: **(x + y)² = x² + y² + 2xy**

Reciprocal sum: **1/x + 1/y = (x + y) / xy**

**Calculations:**

⇒ (1)² = 41 + 2xy

⇒ 1 = 41 + 2xy

⇒ 2xy = 1 − 41

⇒ 2xy = −40

⇒ **xy = −20**

Now, evaluate the required expression:

⇒ 1/x + 1/y = (x + y) / xy

⇒ 1/x + 1/y = 1 / (−20)

⇒ 1/x + 1/y = **−1/20**

**∴ The correct answer is − 1/20.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identities

Standard square identity: (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab and (a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab.

Reciprocal Sum Property

For any non-zero variables x and y, the sum of their reciprocals 1/x + 1/y is always equal to their sum divided by their product: (x + y) / xy.

Sum of Cubes Identity

The identity for cubes is x³ + y³ = (x + y)(x² − xy + y²), which can be solved if the sum and product are known.</p

questions.question: X is twice as good a workman as Y and together they finish a piece of work in 22 days. In how many days will X alone finish the work?

**∴ The correct answer is 33 days.**

questions.question: A pipe can fill a cistern in 20 minutes, but an outlet can empty it in 28 minutes. When both the pipes are opened, in what time is the cistern filled?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume **Total Capacity** of the cistern = LCM of 20 and 28 = 140 units.

Efficiency of **Filling Pipe** = 140 ÷ 20 = +7 units/min.

Efficiency of **Emptying Pipe** = 140 ÷ 28 = −5 units/min.

Net Efficiency when both open = 7 − 5 = 2 units/min.

Time required = Total Capacity ÷ Net Efficiency = 140 ÷ 2 = 70 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 70 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time to fill (x) = 20 min

Time to empty (y) = 28 min

**Formula Used:**

Net Work done in 1 minute = (1/x − 1/y)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ae04e14860cbd44c2ce77bd76bfcf195f68057f8a79848fbef80644fbd7c8cf4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Work done by filling pipe in 1 min = 1/20

⇒ Work done by emptying pipe in 1 min = 1/28

⇒ Net work done in 1 min = 1/20 − 1/28

⇒ Net work = (7 − 5) / 140

⇒ Net work = 2 / 140 = 1 / 70

⇒ Total time taken to fill the cistern = 70 min

The calculated value matches **Option (4)**.

**∴ The correct answer is 70 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combined Rate Formula

If pipe A fills a tank in x hours and pipe B empties it in y hours (where y > x), then the net time taken to fill the tank is (x × y) ÷ (y − x).

Work Sign Convention

In **Pipes and Cisterns**, work done by an inlet pipe is taken as positive (+), and work done by an outlet pipe (leakage) is taken as negative (−).

Efficiency and Time

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If the ratio of time taken by two pipes is a:b, then the ratio of their efficiency is b:a.</p

questions.question: P invests half as much as Q and Q puts in half as much as R in a business. If the monthly proﬁt of Rs. 7000 is shared between them, then what is the share of R?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **investment** of **R** be 4 units.

Then **Q** = 1/2 of 4 = 2 units and **P** = 1/2 of 2 = 1 unit.

Investment Ratio **P : Q : R** = 1 : 2 : 4

Total units = 1 + 2 + 4 = 7 units → Rs. 7000

R's share = 4 units = (7000 ÷ 7) × 4 = Rs. 4000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 4000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total monthly **profit** = Rs. 7000

Investment of **P** = 1/2 × Investment of **Q**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/44985653c058e8081a533d7499df58e30a21669dfc9e3b54905aa2d518ec9f76.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Profit Share ∝ Investment × Time period

Since time is equal for all, Profit ratio = Investment ratio.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let R's investment = R

⇒ Q's investment = R/2

⇒ P's investment = 1/2 × (R/2) = R/4

⇒ Ratio P : Q : R = (R/4) : (R/2) : R

⇒ Multiplying by 4: Ratio = 1 : 2 : 4

⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 1 + 2 + 4 = 7

⇒ R's share = (R's ratio part / Total parts) × Total Profit

⇒ R's share = (4 / 7) × 7000

⇒ R's share = 4 × 1000 = Rs. 4000

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option (4)**.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 4000.**

questions.question: Successive discount of 30%, 20% and 15% are equivalent to a single discount of:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **successive discount formula**: Net Discount = a + b − (a × b)/100

Combine **30%** and **20%**: 30 + 20 − (30 × 20)/100 = 50 − 6 = **44%**

Combine **44%** and **15%**: 44 + 15 − (44 × 15)/100 = 59 − 6.6 = **52.4%**

**∴ The correct answer is 52.4%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Three successive discounts of **30%**, **20%**, and **15%**.

**Formula:** Final Selling Price = Marked Price × (1 − d₁/100) × (1 − d₂/100) × (1 − d₃/100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51ffcb4a5e86019ec0bd7d6b481c2ca61c389494d3dcaf68ac6011501a2fffd0.png] 

⇒ Let **Marked Price (MP)** = 100

⇒ Price after 1st discount (30%) = 100 × (70/100) = 70

⇒ Price after 2ⁿd discount (20%) = 70 × (80/100) = 56

⇒ Price after 3rd discount (15%) = 56 × (85/100) = 47.6

⇒ **Total Discount** = MP − Final SP = 100 − 47.6 = 52.4

⇒ **Equivalent Discount Percentage** = (52.4 / 100) × 100 = 52.4%

**∴ The correct answer is 52.4%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price vs Selling Price

questions.question: A cylindrical tube opened at both the ends is made of iron sheet which is 2 cm thick. If the outer diameter is 16 cm and its length is 100 cm, find how many cubic centimeters of iron has been used in making the tube ?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Outer radius R = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 cm, Inner radius r = 8 − 2 = 6 cm

Volume of iron = π × (R + r) × (R − r) × h

Volume = (22/7) × (8 + 6) × (8 − 6) × 100

Volume = (22/7) × 14 × 2 × 100 = 8800 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 8800 cm³.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Outer diameter** (D) = 16 cm

**Thickness** (t) = 2 cm

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Outer radius** (R) = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 cm

⇒ **Inner radius** (r) = R − thickness = 8 − 2 = 6 cm

⇒ **Volume of iron** = (22/7) × (8² − 6²) × 100

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × (64 − 36) × 100

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 28 × 100

⇒ Volume = 22 × 4 × 100 = 8800 cm³

questions.question: Sum of the digits of the smallest four digit number, which when divided by 12, 15 and 20, leaves a remainder in each case is 3:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the **LCM** of 12, 15, and 20, which is **60**.

The smallest **4-digit number** is 1000. Divide 1000 by 60 to find the next multiple.

1000 ÷ 60 gives a remainder of 40. Next multiple = 1000 + (60 − 40) = **1020**.

Add the **remainder 3**: 1020 + 3 = **1023**.

Sum of digits = 1 + 0 + 2 + 3 = **6**.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Divisors = 12, 15, 20 | Remainder = 3 | Condition = Smallest 4-digit number.

**Formula Used:** Number (N) = (LCM × k) + Remainder

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2e3259e4130066fd0dec02c7fa16f65b243ec19e2cb70a1abf5fe1b016811adf.png] 

⇒ **Step 1:** Calculate LCM of 12, 15, and 20.

⇒ 12 = 2² × 3 | 15 = 3 × 5 | 20 = 2² × 5

⇒ LCM = 2² × 3 × 5 = 60

⇒ **Step 2:** Find the smallest 4-digit multiple of 60.

⇒ Smallest 4-digit number = 1000

⇒ 1000 ÷ 60 ⇒ Quotient = 16, Remainder = 40

⇒ Next multiple = 60 × (16 + 1) = 60 × 17 = 1020

⇒ **Step 3:** Calculate the final number and sum of digits.

⇒ Number = 1020 + 3 = 1023

⇒ Sum of digits = 1 + 0 + 2 + 3 = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM Method for Remainders

When a number leaves the same **remainder (r)** when divided by divisors x, y, and z, the general form is N = LCM(x, y, z) × k + r.

Smallest 4-Digit Number Property

To find a specific multiple near a limit, divide the limit by the **LCM** and adjust by adding the difference (LCM − remainder).

Sum of Digits Rule

The sum of digits is used in **divisibility rules** for 3 and 9; a number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3.</p

questions.question: In still water, Rajni can row 135 km in 7.5 hours, while she can row 48 km upstream in 4 hours. What is the speed of the current in km/hr?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Still water speed** = 135 ÷ 7.5 = 18 km/hr

**Upstream speed** = 48 ÷ 4 = 12 km/hr

**Speed of current** = Still water speed − Upstream speed

Speed of current = 18 − 12 = 6 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 6 km/hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance covered in **still water** = 135 km

Time taken in **still water** = 7.5 hr

Distance covered **upstream** = 48 km

Time taken **upstream** = 4 hr

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Upstream Speed** (vᵤₚ) = **Speed in still water** (u) − **Speed of current** (v)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/abdf37f760ce03c7b9359b9b33330f164a5df3b267990f73bc344b8d84a42cdc.png] 

⇒ **Speed of Rajni** in **still water** (u) = 135 / 7.5

⇒ u = 18 km/hr

⇒ **Upstream speed** (vᵤₚ) = 48 / 4

⇒ vᵤₚ = 12 km/hr

⇒ According to the formula: vᵤₚ = u − v

⇒ 12 = 18 − v

⇒ v = 18 − 12

⇒ v = 6 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 6 km/hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Downstream Speed

When the boat moves in the same direction as the stream, the effective speed is the sum of the boat speed and current speed: vdₒwₙ = u + v.

Speed of Current (v) from Net Speeds

The current speed can be calculated directly if both downstream and upstream speeds are known: v = (vdₒwₙ − vᵤₚ) ÷ 2.

Still Water Speed (u) from Net Speeds

The speed of the boat in still water is the average of the downstream and upstream speeds: u = (vdₒwₙ + vᵤₚ) ÷ 2.</p
